monday.label: Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling
monday.description: Local arts scene, festivals, creative economy, media, and cultural tech
monday.theme_description: Today we explore how Cariboo and rural BC communities create, preserve, and share culture — from festivals and community radio to digital archives and open-source arts tools. We're looking for stories where creativity meets technology in small-town contexts, and where local artists and storytellers are finding new ways to reach audiences beyond geography.
monday.scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling' — how communities create, preserve, and share culture, with particular interest in the Cariboo and rural BC.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-14: medical and health research with no cultural angle; resource-economy stories with no cultural framing; wildlife and nature stories without a creative or community-media context; data centre and AI investment news; geopolitical conflict, war, and crime coverage; financial market stories.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. A Cariboo tie raises a score but is NOT required to reach the top band: judge on the strength of the arts/culture/storytelling reporting first.
- 80-100: Excellent arts, culture, or storytelling journalism. Cariboo/Williams Lake arts news lands here (arts council grants, murals, local festivals, Indigenous film, community theatre, heritage programs, a Cariboo author or artist honoured) — and so does outstanding national or international cultural reporting with real depth.
- 55-79: Solid arts/culture/media journalism. Rural BC and Canadian cultural coverage, CBC Arts features, regional festivals, community media projects, heritage preservation, creative-economy stories, digital storytelling tools and platforms, community media tech (podcasting, streaming, local publishing), animation and film production. Most genuine cultural journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Mainstream entertainment-industry coverage with modest substance (awards-show results, film/TV/music business news, publishing trade news).
- 15-29: Tangentially creative — a tech feature touching media/publishing/streaming, or Cariboo civic news with no arts angle.

ANCHORS: 'Repatriated Tŝilhqot'in baskets arrive in Williams Lake from Brooklyn Museum' → 95. 'How a BC First Nation is digitizing its oral histories' → 80. 'CBC Arts: the quiet revival of small-town prairie theatre' → 68. 'Netflix reports Q3 subscriber growth' → 20.

Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

tuesday.label: Working Lands & Industry
tuesday.description: Cariboo forestry, ranching, mining, agriculture — tech in the resource economy
tuesday.theme_description: Today's focus is the resource economy that defines the Cariboo — forestry, ranching, mining, and the agricultural technology helping these industries adapt and modernize. We're looking for stories about the people and innovations keeping rural BC's working landscape viable, including tensions between resource extraction and long-term stewardship, and the technology bridging both.
tuesday.scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Working Lands & Industry' — forestry, ranching, mining, and agriculture, the resource economy that defines the Cariboo and rural BC.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-14: geopolitical and war news with no resource-economy connection; consumer tech and gadget reviews; wildlife content with no agricultural or working-lands relevance; crime and judicial news unrelated to resource industries; financial market and stock ticker stories.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. Trade-press journalism counts fully: equipment, markets, and operations coverage is a real fit, not a near-zero. A BC tie raises a score but is NOT required to reach the top band.
- 80-100: Excellent working-lands journalism. BC/Cariboo forestry, ranching, mining, and agriculture stories land here (mill closures, beetle kill, BCTS, Cariboo ranchers and water rights, local mine operations, Cariboo Cattlemen) — and so does outstanding national trade reporting with real operational or economic depth.
- 55-79: Solid resource-economy journalism anywhere in Canada or beyond — Western Producer or Northern Miner-style coverage of farm machinery, harvest technology, livestock and commodity markets, mining operations and exploration, AgTech and precision agriculture, silviculture, sawmills, drone survey work, mine automation, and labour/workforce stories in these industries. Most genuine trade journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Broader agriculture, forestry, or mining news with clear working-lands relevance but thin reporting — general farm economics, international resource-industry briefs, climate impacts on working lands.
- 15-29: Tangential mentions — a business, policy, or science story that touches forestry/agriculture/mining in passing, or Cariboo civic news unrelated to working lands.

ANCHORS: 'Williams Lake sawmill cuts second shift as beetle-kill supply dwindles' → 95. 'New John Deere baler cuts hay-drying time by a third' → 70. 'Cattle futures slip on weaker export demand' → 60. 'Global copper prices hit two-year high' → 40.

Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

wednesday.label: Repair Culture & Practical Tech
wednesday.description: Right to repair, gear that outlasts the manufacturer, DIY fixes, maker projects, and tools built to last
wednesday.theme_description: Today is about things you can fix, keep running, and pass on — repair culture, right-to-repair wins and setbacks, gear that outlives its manufacturer's support window, and the maker ethos of building to last rather than building to replace. We're interested in tools, devices, and projects where longevity, repairability, and self-sufficiency intersect, especially in rural and off-grid contexts where you can't just run to a repair shop.
wednesday.scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Repair Culture & Practical Tech' — the right to repair movement, gear that outlasts its manufacturer, DIY fixes, and tools built for longevity.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-9: geopolitical conflict; natural disasters without an engineering or preparedness angle; wildlife and conservation; working-lands policy; Indigenous governance; science discoveries with no DIY or hardware relevance; financial market news.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. Hands-on hardware journalism counts fully even without an explicit right-to-repair hook.
- 80-100: Directly about repairability — right-to-repair legislation wins and losses, iFixit-style teardowns scoring repairability, gear designed for user serviceability, products outliving manufacturer support and how owners keep them running, permacomputing, vintage hardware still in active use, open-source hardware, Rossmann-style repair advocacy, 3D-printed replacement parts, battery replacement guides, rural and off-grid repair self-sufficiency.
- 55-79: Hands-on maker and DIY content — builds, modifications, hardware hacks, workshop projects, practical electronics guides with real technical depth, 3D printing hardware and filament, off-grid and solar gear, home lab hardware, tools and workshop equipment, battery and power tech. Most genuine hands-on hardware journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Gadget and device reviews with some technical substance; consumer electronics touching software longevity or ecosystem lock-in; hardware whose selling point is open firmware or modular design.
- 10-29: Surface-level product announcements, gadget speculation, leaked specs, general tech news with no hardware or repair angle.

ANCHORS: 'Framework Laptop 16 teardown: a 9/10 repairability score' → 98. 'Oregon's right-to-repair law takes effect' → 92. 'Building a solar-powered Raspberry Pi weather station' → 68. 'Samsung teases thinner bezels on next Galaxy' → 15.

Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

thursday.label: Indigenous Lands & Innovation
thursday.description: Tŝilhqot'in, Secwépemc, Dakelh — language, governance, land stewardship, and tech
thursday.theme_description: Today we explore how Cariboo and BC Indigenous nations are using technology on their own terms — for language revitalization, land stewardship, cultural preservation, and self-determined governance. We're looking for stories that centre Indigenous voices and leadership in innovation, where technology serves community sovereignty rather than replacing it.
thursday.scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Indigenous Lands & Innovation' — Indigenous nations using technology, governance, and stewardship on their own terms.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-9: geopolitical and war news with no Indigenous rights angle; general wildfire and wildlife-service updates not led by or directly affecting Indigenous communities or guardians; provincial forestry and environmental policy with no explicit First Nations involvement; consumer tech and gadget reviews; science with no Indigenous stewardship or sovereignty context; crime and judicial news unrelated to Indigenous rights.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. Indigenous-led journalism on governance, rights, and self-determination is a strong fit on its own: a technology hook raises a score but is NOT required to reach the top band.
- 80-100: Excellent Indigenous-led reporting. Cariboo stories bridging governance or culture AND technology land here (Tŝilhqot'in/Secwépemc/Dakelh language revitalization tech, guardian programs using sensors and drones, GIS land mapping, Indigenous-led connectivity, digital heritage projects) — and so does outstanding national coverage of sovereignty, treaty, and land rights.
- 55-79: Solid pan-Canadian Indigenous governance, sovereignty, land rights, treaty, or reconciliation journalism — APTN, Eagle Feather News, or IndigiNews-style coverage of First Nations governance, MMIWG, land claims, self-determination, and Indigenous-led services. Most Indigenous governance journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Indigenous cultural, community, or human-interest stories (awards, events, ceremonies) with limited governance substance, or BC land-stewardship and environmental stories with meaningful First Nations involvement.
- 10-29: General BC land, environmental, or forestry stories that mention Indigenous communities only in passing.

ANCHORS: 'Tŝilhqot'in Nation launches drone-based caribou monitoring on title lands' → 98. 'First Nations leaders reject BC's revised land-title framework' → 75. 'Secwépemc language app reaches 1,000 learners' → 88. 'BC Wildfire Service updates evacuation alerts for the Interior' → 8.

Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

friday.label: Wild Spaces & Outdoor Life
friday.description: Chilcotin wilderness, backcountry recreation, conservation tech, wildfire and climate
friday.theme_description: Today we head into the wild — the Chilcotin (chil-KOH-tin) plateau, river valleys, and backcountry that define the Cariboo experience. We're covering the technology helping monitor, protect, and navigate these landscapes: wildfire detection, wildlife tracking, satellite communication, and the tools keeping backcountry travellers safe and conservationists informed.
friday.scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Wild Spaces & Outdoor Life' through a RURAL TECH AND INNOVATION lens. Strong fits include: wildfire detection tech and BC Wildfire monitoring systems, satellite/drone surveillance for Chilcotin wilderness, wildlife tracking and conservation technology, watershed sensors and salmon habitat monitoring, weather stations and climate tracking in backcountry, avalanche forecasting tech, trail mapping and GPS systems, outdoor recreation apps and connectivity, backcountry communication devices (satellite messengers, Meshtastic), flood/drought prediction systems, remote cameras for wildlife research, and how technology helps manage and protect Cariboo wild spaces. Prefer articles that bridge wilderness/conservation AND technology. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): prehistoric and ancient biology (fossils, palaeontology, deep-time creatures) with no contemporary conservation technology angle — these belong to Sunday's Science theme; AI and data centre infrastructure stories about business strategy, investment, or corporate politics rather than direct wilderness, ecosystem, or land-use impact in BC; geopolitical conflict, war, and crime news with no outdoor or conservation relevance; consumer tech reviews and financial market stories; general political and judicial news. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

saturday.label: Cariboo Local Affairs
saturday.description: Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola — community stories and digital equity
saturday.theme_description: Today is all about the Cariboo-Chilcotin (chil-KOH-tin) region: the decisions, events, and conversations happening in Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola, and the surrounding region. We're covering local government, community life, economic stories, and the digital equity challenges that shape what it means to live and work in rural BC.
saturday.scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Cariboo Voices & Local News' — stories FROM and ABOUT the Cariboo-Chilcotin region and its communities. Score 80-100 for articles directly covering: news and events in Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola, Horsefly, Likely, Anahim Lake, Alexis Creek, or the Cariboo Regional District; local government and civic decisions (City of Williams Lake, City of Quesnel, CRD, District of 100 Mile House); local health services and emergency closures; local economy, businesses, and community programs; Cariboo arts, culture, and community events; AND digital equity, rural internet access (fiber, fixed wireless, Starlink), and connectivity serving these specific communities. Articles from local Cariboo news sources (mycariboonow.com, wltribune.com, quesnelobserver.com, 100milefreepress.net, cfjctoday.com) covering Cariboo community life should score 65-85. Score 50-79 for: BC provincial news directly affecting Cariboo communities, rural Canadian community stories closely paralleling Cariboo life, digital equity and rural internet broadly. Score 20-49 for: general BC news that may affect rural areas, broader rural Canada topics without specific Cariboo tie-in. Score 0-19 for: national/international news without Cariboo relevance, pure tech or entertainment with no community angle. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): international geopolitical and war news with no Cariboo tie-in; science discoveries without a local community connection; consumer tech reviews and gadget guides; wildlife and conservation stories not involving Cariboo communities or First Nations; BC provincial news without direct Cariboo-region relevance. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

sunday.label: Science, Wonder & the Natural World
sunday.description: Scientific discovery, natural phenomena, ecology, and the curiosity behind how our world works — grounded in the landscapes and living systems of the Cariboo
sunday.theme_description: Today we look at scientific discovery and the natural world — from ecology and wildlife research to astronomy and deep-sea biology. We're grounding these stories in the landscapes and living systems of the Cariboo: what salmon runs, boreal forest research, or species-at-risk studies tell us about the wild places we live beside. We're after stories that inspire curiosity and wonder about how the world works.
sunday.scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Science, Wonder & the Natural World' — scientific discovery, ecology, natural phenomena, and the curiosity-driven study of living systems. Strong fits include: wildlife biology and species research, ecology studies and biodiversity findings, watershed and salmon research relevant to BC, astronomy and space science, new species discoveries, citizen science projects, natural history stories, wildfire science and forest ecology, climate science findings (not just policy), geology, evolution, and deep-time Earth stories, and any scientific research grounded in BC or Cariboo landscapes and ecosystems. Prefer articles that convey genuine curiosity and discovery — the 'how' and 'why' of the natural world. Score 70–90 for: prehistoric life and palaeontology (ancient oceans, Cretaceous ecology, deep-time species), new species discoveries in ocean or remote environments, deep-sea biology, evolutionary biology findings, natural history stories with a strong sense of wonder, and field research grounded in BC ecosystems. Penalise (score 0–30): consumer health and pharmaceutical research without ecology or natural-world context; pure policy and advocacy news; technology business stories without a science or ecology angle; human interest and viral news without scientific substance; geopolitical and crime news. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.
